Container.Name: tldw-webui
Container.Overview: tl;dw (Too Long, Didn't Watch) - the browser frontend, a Next.js app that talks to the tl;dw API server. THREE CONTAINERS, STARTED IN ORDER: tldw-redis first, then tldw-server, then tldw-webui. There is no template equivalent of compose depends_on, so nothing enforces that ordering for you. ⚠️ REQUIRES A ONE-TIME MANUAL NETWORK SETUP BEFORE THIS WORKS: the published image has its API origin (http://app:8000) compiled into the build output rather than read from the environment (unraid-templates#55), so no field here can wire it - you must create a user-defined Docker network, set BOTH this container's and tldw-server's Network field to it at creation, and add --network-alias=app to tldw-server's Extra Parameters. Skip any of the three and the container starts and renders but every API call silently goes nowhere - see this template's header comment for the exact steps. The same network is the one tldw-redis and tldw-server share (Docker must preserve user-defined networks across updates - Unraid: Settings > Docker). The UI also needs tldw-server's SINGLE_USER_API_KEY entered in it, and tldw-server's MCP_ALLOWED_IPS set to that network, or the UI reports the backend unavailable. Two environment variables are inert for the same build-time-baked reason and are deliberately not offered as fields: the API origin above, and NEXT_PUBLIC_TLDW_DEPLOYMENT_MODE. STORAGE: none - this container is stateless, nothing in the published image references a persistent path. IMAGE TAG: upstream publishes no release-numbered tag for this image, only main and per-commit sha-* tags; this template pins sha-7a23be3, verified against the live GHCR tags API - re-check before assuming it is still current if this has sat a while. EXPOSURE: publishing the port below makes this reachable on your LAN; anything further (a domain, reverse proxy, TLS) is ordinary hostname routing, not something this template does - that is a separate, later step for whoever administers your network, not part of getting this container running.
Container.Description: tl;dw browser frontend. Needs tldw-redis + tldw-server running first, AND a one-time manual network-alias setup (see the template's own header/Overview) or every API call silently goes nowhere.

Config.Name: HTTP Port
Config.Description: Host port for the web UI. The container always listens on 3000 internally - change the host side only. The default here is deliberately not 3000, a popular port, so a neutral value avoids a collision on a busy host. ⚠️ THIS CONTAINER DOES NOTHING USEFUL UNTIL A ONE-TIME MANUAL NETWORK SETUP IS DONE: create a user-defined Docker network, set both this container's AND tldw-server's Network field to it (at creation - the Network dropdown only lists networks that already exist), and add --network-alias=app to tldw-server's Extra Parameters. The published image has its API origin compiled in at build time (unraid-templates#55) rather than read from any variable, so skipping this leaves a UI that renders and silently talks to nothing. No volume is offered on this template - it is stateless.
